title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that there is not a Certified Food Protection Manager present during the inspection. PICs were notified -- their previous certification recently expired. PICs plan to renew their CFPM. Ensure that the PICs are CFPMs who are always present when food preparation is happening.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil residues on the following:
(i) the interior of the soda machine nozzles. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and cleaned the nozzles during the inspection until they were clean to sight and touch.
(ii) inside the ice machine. PIC was informed and instructed to clean and maintain the machine regularly to prevent contamination.
Ensure food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that several sanitizer buckets did not have a measureable amount of sanitizer in them - 0ppm (Chlorine) for the sanitizer bucket in the bar and 0ppm (quaternary ammonium) for the sanitizer buckets in the dish area. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and remade the buckets so that they measured a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer: 100ppm (Cl) for the bar sanitizer bucket made from bleach and water (1 capful of bleach to 1 gallon of water); and 200pm (quat) for the dish room sanitizer buckets (filled from the dispenser over the mop sink). Ensure that sanitizers are used per manufacturer instructions so that there is a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer for food-contact surfaces: 50-200 ppm for Chlorine-based sanitizer and 200-400ppm for quaternary ammonium.
citation_text: 4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed a gap between the exterior door and door frame so that there was visible daylight along the bottom of the door. PIC was informed and will repair the door or attach a barrier to avoid entry of insects, rodents and other animals.
citation_text: 6-202.16 Exterior Walls and Roofs, Protective Barrier. Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed an opened can of tomato purée that is stored in a cooler in its original can without a cover. Opened cans of food are not storage containers (once opened, the can itself can be source of potential contamination, especially if the food item is acidic). CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the product was removed from the cooler so that it could be repackaged in a cleanable container. Ensure that food is protected from potential contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed the scoop in the chips in the server area stored with the handle touching the chips. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the scoop was moved to sit on top of the chip container where the handle does not touch the food. Since the handle is touched by bare hands it must be stored above the top of food. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed single-use containers stored on top of the prep cooler upright where the food-contact surfaces are exposed to debris from above. CORRECTED: Staff were informed and inverted the containers so that the food-contact surfaces were protected from contamination. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are protected by either inversion or cover from a closed shelf or packaging.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed no lids on the trash cans in the women's restroom. PIC was made aware and will ensure that the women’s stalls each have covered trash receptacles.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(i) Observed a broken gasket in the hot box in the kitchen; PIC was informed and will repair the gasket. 
(ii) Observed the mop sink needs to be resealed to the wall as the original seal has crumbled; PIC was informed and will get the mop sink resealed.
Ensure that all physical facilities are in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.  [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mops drying on the floor in the mens rooms where they cannot drain or air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and moved the mops to hang above the mop sink where they can air-dry. PIC and Inspector also discussed that wet mops can sit in the upper basket of a mop bucket so they can drain and air-dry without contaminating the surrounding area. Ensure that after use mops are placed so that they can air-dry without soiling walls, floors, equipment, or supplies.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were dirty dishes observed in the basin of the handwashing sink. The dishes were removed and placed inside of the ware washing sink to correct the violation. Ensure that the handwashing sink remains unobstructed to allow easy access for employees to wash hands.
citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were raw beef patties stored above ready to eat foods inside of the main cooler. The RTE foods included veggies, sauces, and cheeses. Discussed with the PIC and the beef was moved to the bottom shelf of the cooler to correct the violation. Ensure that raw meats are always stored beneath RTE foods to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There is observed to not be a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present in the facility during today’s inspection. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was observed to be ice that had been dumped in the handwashing sink at the bar. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that handwashing sinks are only used for their intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The drinking straws in the bar area were observed unwrapped and stored in close proximity to consumers. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the containers of straws to be behind the bar counter. Ensure that unwrapped straws are either stored behind the counter where they are controlled by employees or purchase wrapped straws for consumers.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

comment:

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. SECOND REPEAT- The handwashing sink to the right of the cook-line is observed to be in need of being re-sealed. 
2. SECOND REPEAT- The table to the left of the dish machine is in need of being sealed to the wall.

citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There was observed to be a phone charging on the top of the preparation cooler on the cook-line. There was also observed to be personal canned drinks in the double-door cooler in between trays of food for the facility. Discussed making sure to store personal items in a designated area to prevent contamination to food-contact surfaces and food for the facility. It is recommended to have a bucket on the bottom shelf of a cooler labeled “Personal” for employee food and drinks.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival, there weren’t any employees who were food manager certified. Shortly throughout the visit, a CFPM arrived to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always an employee present who holds a manger’s certification if operating during business hours.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were at least two containers of salad dressings that lacked proper date marking inside of the dressing cooler. The items included tartar sauce and chipotle mayonnaise. Discussed with the PIC that in house dressings require date marking if being cold held longer than 24 hours. Ensure that dressings are date marked to make sure that they are getting used within the seven day timeframe.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed single service to go containers stored with the food contact surfaces not inverted. Discussed with the PIC and the containers were properly inverted to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always faced downward to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- Floor under dish machine’s drainboard was observed with accumulated food debris
- Floor in back-stock area (where bread rack is stored) was observed with accumulated food debris
Be sure to sweep the above mentioned areas as frequent as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed that a sanitizing solution was not available when Inspector arrived despite food preparation having just started. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and made a sanitizing bucket that tested at 100ppm (Chlorine), a safe and effective concentration of that sanitizer (Chlorine should be between 50-200ppm). Inspector discussed with the PIC that a sanitizing solution should be available at all times during food preparation for sanitizing surfaces, not just during times of warewashing. Ensure that a sanitizing solution is available for use for all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Observed that there was not a PIC present who demonstrated knowledge on proper warewashing procedures. When asked, PIC explained that the 2-compartment sink is used for warewashing, with wash and rinse happening in the two basins, then the sink is emptied and reset for sanitizing. A 3-compartment sink is available for warewashing in the meat room. All warewashing should take place there, where one basin each can be designated for wash, rinse, and sanitize. Ensure that the PIC demonstrates knowledge of correct sanitizing procedures.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(11) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include: (11) Explaining correct procedures for cleaning and SANITIZING UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that there was a not a staff member who had a Certified Food Protection Manager certification on the premises. PIC was notified. Ensure that a CFPM is on the premises at all times when food preparation can occur.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed ground meat stored over whole meat, and raw meat was stored above cured ready-to-eat meat in the deli meat 4-door display cooler. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and the meats in that cooler were moved so that RTE meat was stored above whole meat, and whole meat was stored above ground meat. Inspector provided educational handouts about storage order. Meats of different final cooking temperatures can be stored side-by-side as long as they are kept separate and they are not stored improperly over another item. Ensure that animal proteins are always stored according to internal cooking temperatures to avoid contamination: ready-to-eat foods (no cooking required/ pre-cooked), above whole meat (145 F), above ground meat (155 F), above chicken and turkey (165 F).
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following areas that have an accumulation of soils:
(i) the walk-in cooler fans are dusty.
(ii) the walk-in freezer has significant ice accumulation.
PIC was notified that these areas need to be cleaned with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues so that they are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the trash receptacle in the women’s bathroom does not have a lid. PIC was notified that all bathroom stalls that are used by women have to have a covered trash receptacle. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have a covered trash can.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the coving along the wall in the meat department has come away from the wall and needs to be repaired. PIC was notified. Ensure that walls are coved and sealed to the floor.
citation_text: 6-201.13(B) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED. [C]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspectors observed that there is not an ambient thermometer in the refrigerator in the kitchen and the ambient thermometer in the storage room cooler is not functional. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that all cold and hot holding units have a functional ambient thermometer in them to make sure that TCS foods are being properly cold or hot held.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: One of the PICs was observed to use the handwashing sink to fill the sanitizer bucket. CORRECTED- The PICs were both educated that handwashing sinks should only be used for the intended purpose of handwashing and that the triple sink should be used instead to fill the bucket. Ensure that handwashing sinks are only used for the purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIRD REPEAT- There was a pan of raw beef above a container of carrots in the bottom of the preparation cooler. CORRECTED- The beef was moved to the bottom and the carrots were moved above the raw beef. Due to this being a third repeat violation, the inspector will bring the health educator to the facility for education on storage order. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed that single-service and single-use articles and utensils were stored with the food-contact surfaces upright, including plastic cutlery single-use food cartons and nacho cheese holders. Customers and staff could potentially touch multiple food-contact surfaces when reaching for a utensil or a carton. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and utensils were flipped so that only there handles were upright, and cartons were flipped or placed underneath a closed shelf to protect the food-contact surfaces from debris from above. PIC and Inspector discussed additional ways that single-use utensils could be stored, including horizontal in either cleanable or disposable containers, as long as all the utensils are facing the same direction, so only handles will be touched when dispensed. Ensure that single-service and single-use utensils and articles are stored such that contamination of food-contact surfaces is prevented.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the individual trash receptacles in the stalls of the women’s bathroom do not have lids/covers. PIC was notified and Inspector discussed that covered trash receptacles are required in bathroom facilities used by women per IL Food Code, as it is more hygienic and protects plumbing from improperly flushed items. Inspector also discussed that upcoming Food Code updates (based on the 2026 FDA Food Code) will expand this need to all bathroom stalls, not just bathrooms used by women. Ensure all toilet rooms used by women have covered trash receptacles.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

PIC was notified. Ensure that the premises is free of items that are unnecessary to the operation such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used.

comment: Caulk frontline counter to the wall where tile was replaced.

comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of soil and food debris on the shield and plunger of the milkshake machine. The PIC was informed and the machine was cleaned and sanitized to sight and touch. Ensure staff are cleaning food contact surfaces frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 
Observed that facility does not have written procedures for Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events(Norovirus) and also does not have proper chemical to assist with cleaning a norovirus event. PIC was made aware and written procedures was provided by inspectors and PIC assured that facility will purchase EPA certified bleach soon. Ensure that having proper EPA certified chemical and written procedures are available to respond to a vomit/diarrheal event. 

Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
4-703.11(C) 
REPEAT
The sanitizer bucket in the front side near soda machine tested at 0ppm (chlorine).The facility has QUAT available and the bucket was remade and tested at 400ppm(quat). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are tested after they are prepared to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(2) Hot Water and Chemical. citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be stored in mop bucket with soiled mop water present. Discussed with PIC, mop water will be discarded and mop will be stored in a way that allows for air drying. Ensure mop is stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the temperature-sensitive tape for the dish washer the facility uses is for 180 F, which means the water inside the dish washer is so hot that it is more steam than water when it hits the dishes. PIC states the facility normally uses a heavy wash cycle. Inspector measured the dish machine using a final temperature registering plate to be 151 F on the top rack, which is too low for sanitizing. Inspector used 160 F temperature-sensitive tape on the bottom rack which showed final temperatures of 160 F or above. PIC used 180 F temperature-sensitive tape on the bottom rack which showed final temperatures of 180 F or above. Inspector and PIC discussed using 160-170-180 F temperature-sensitive tape or a final temperature measuring plate to determine what is the optimal wash cycle and placement for dish sanitizing. Ensure that mechanical warewashing sanitizing water is between 160-170 F.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: Observed that the prep sink and 3 handwashing sinks in the classroom had low hot water pressure. PICs were notified and they discussed repairs with the custodian. Ensure that water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures.
citation_text: 5-103.12 Pressure. Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water supplied as specified under 5-104.12(A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure. [Pf]

citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

citation_text:

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 
Observed employee changing gloves without washing hands. CORRECTED- Inspector noticed and provided education.Ensure proper handwashing procedures are always followed.

When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 3 cans of food (mushrooms X2 and green beans) to contain significant dents along the seams. CORRECTED- cans were segregated from those for service to be returned to food supplier for credit. Ensure hermetically sealed cans are inspected for dents along the seams, and large dents along the body while stocking dry storage. Cans that are dented along the seams may allow for the entry and harborage of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.[Pf]

comment: FIRST REPEAT: The sanitizer bucket used for wiping food contact surfaces was observed to have no measurable sanitizer concentration. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made at a frequency to hold the concentration as recommended by the manufacterer's label (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The gallons of milk in the single standing cooler at the kitchen’s entry were probed to have an internal temperatures between 48-50F. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) stated the milk had been delivered the previous day, so the milk (9 gallons) was discarded. A prune juice that was opened to take measure its internal temperature (labeled “refrigerate after opening”) was moved to the working 3 door cooler. Ensure all animal proteins, cut tomatoes and melons, and items labeled “keep refrigerated” are kept at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed opened milk, cut tomatoes, and prepared salads to lack date marking. CORRECTED- items were opened or prepared the previous day, and marked with the corresponding date. Ensure all ready to eat, temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are marked with a date after preparation/ thawing/ opening, to be used or discarded within seven days to prevent the growth and harborage of Listeria. The day of opening/ thawing/ preparation counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed an open gallon of milk with a 5/24 expiration date in the memory care refrigerator. CORRECTED- the milk was discarded. Ensure milk is DATE MARKED once opened, to be used or discarded within seven days of date marking, OR by the expiration date, whichever comes first.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

comment: The standing single cooler at the kitchen’s entry was observed to have an ambient temperature of approximately 50F. The PIC stated the unit had been serviced approximately two weeks ago. citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.

citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector observed the prep table on the service line to be damaged and temporarily protected with tape. The broken edge of the prep table is very sharp, and poses a hazard to staff. However, the tape is not food-safe and therefore cannot remain on the surface. Ensure the prep table is replaced to prevent food safety or employee safety hazards. 

FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector observed the triple sink in the food preparation space to be damaged and tipping away from the wall. Due to the incorrect angle of the sink basin, water is collecting and standing in the basin. Ensure this is repaired to prevent water retention in the sink. 

SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector also observed the triple sink to be cracked between two basins. This allows water to leak from the sink to the floor.

Ensure these items are repaired prior to the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant of both hand sinks to be damaged. This damage has resulted in a crevice between the sink and wall which allows for moisture to accumulate. The sinks must be maintained so that they are easily cleanable. Ensure the sealant is replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION - Observed interior of coolers to be soiled with food debris. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil.

Inspector observed the shelving above the triple sink to be heavily soiled. As clean dishes are stored on this shelf, this poses a contamination risk. Ensure the shelf is clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection. 

Inspector observed the shelving in the walk-in cooler to be soiled with mold. The moisture in the walk-in cooler is contributing to this issue. Ensure the cooler is repaired and deep cleaned/sanitized prior to the next routine inspection. 

Inspector observed the triple sink to be soiled with black debris. This debris is building up around the sanitizer and detergent dispenser as well as the right corner of the sink. The right corner of the sink is not graded correctly, resulting in water collecting near the wall and pouring down the wall to the floor. This area is heavily soiled. Ensure the sink is cleaned, sanitized, and repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector observed the following areas in need of a deep cleaning:
1. Floor under stoves and fryers
2. Floors of dish area
3. Floors of walk-in cooler

Inspector also observed the vent of the walk-in cooler to be soiled with dust and debris.

 Ensure facility has been deep cleaned prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed two staff members on site that did not have a valid food handler’s certification. The PIC is aware of the issue. Qdoba has recently changed policy to pay for food handler’s certification for staff. Ensure all employees have food handler’s certification prior to the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food separated and protected.

Ensure that raw proteins are arranged by cooking temperature to protect food items from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The cooler drawers under the grill in the facility are observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. The following food items were probed: 
- Three pans of steak: probed to be at 48F, 50F, and 52F. 
- A pan of chicken: 46F. 
- A pan of riblets: 50F. 
- A pan of cooked fettuccini noodles: 49F. 
CORRECTED- These items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. A pan of cooked Penne noodles were moved into another cooler, due to only being placed in the cooler about 30 minutes prior. It is recommended to check temperatures of coolers more frequently. Ensure that TCS foods are being cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

comment: The cooler drawers under the grill were observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. TCS food items that were above 41F were voluntarily discarded by the PIC (see violation #22). A follow up is scheduled for 6/8/2026 to ensure that the cooler drawers have been repaired and are cold holding at 41F or below. Ensure that equipment used for cold and hot holding is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There are observed to be flies next to the soda syrup boxes in the back of facility that are flying around a large puddle of pooling water. A follow up is scheduled on 6/8/2026 to ensure that the flies have been eliminated and the pooling water has been cleaned up. Ensure that pest control is routinely treating the facility, the facility is being maintained cleaned, and water is not allowed to pool to prevent pest harborage conditions.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

comment:

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was a phone observed to be stored on top of a lid to a bread container. CORRECTED- The PIC removed the phone and educated the employee. Phones hold a significant amount of bacteria and should never be stored on a food-contact surface. Ensure that employee items are stored separately to avoid contaminating food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.

citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A probe thermometer placed in an empty pan in the cooler read 54F. The cooler's digital read-out indicates 54F. citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.
