title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed no hand washing sign present at the bar/kitchen hand sink or two bathroom hand sinks. The PIC was informed and hand washing signs were provided. Ensure these signs are posted by all three handwashing sinks and are clearly visible for all staff to view.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the PIC use the bar/kitchen hand sink to empty/refill the sanitizer bucket. The bucket was temporarily stored in the sink basin. Education was conducted regarding hand sinks. Ensure hand sinks are for hand washing only. Hand sinks cannot be obstructed under any conditions, especially since the facility only has one sink for the bar and kitchen.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the bar/kitchen sanitizer bucket measure 50ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed that the sanitizer was not strong enough, and the bucket was replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure the bucket is monitored for proper chemical concentration. The sanitizer will weaken over time and must be replaced frequently.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with a black debris. The PIC was informed that the ice machine needs to be deep cleaned and sanitized. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure the ice machine is clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed a container of pico de gallo in the prep cooler top measure 55F with the infrared probe. The pico de gallo was stored in a plastic container within a metal container in the cooler. This “doubling” prevents adequate air movement and refrigeration of the container. Since the pico de gallo had no date mark and the PIC did not know when the item was prepared, the container was discarded. Ensure proper cold holding is monitored with a stem thermometer. Storage in the prep cooler needs to promote proper cooling. A spot check will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are stored properly in the cooler and maintaining a temperature of 41F or less at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food items to be missing a date mark:

1. Pico de gallo
2. Shrimp
3. Sausage
4. Pork pieces

The PIC was informed that all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) and ready-to-eat (RTE) foods must be date marked within 24 hours of opening/prepping. These items must be discarded within 7 days of marking. A handout was provided with extra details regarding proper date marking methods. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure proper date marking practices are taking place in the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no ambient thermometers stored in the prep cooler or upright cooler in the kitchen. The PIC was informed and plans to acquire thermometers for the cooler. Ensure all coolers have ambient thermometers prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed multiple dishes to be stored on a top shelf with their food contact surfaces exposed to splash and dust. The PIC was informed that the items need to be inverted to prevent contamination. Ensure these items are properly stored prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia test strips available at the facility. Quaternary ammonia is in use as sanitizer in both the sanitizer buckets and triple sink. The PIC was informed and stated she could not find the test strips. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to confirm test strip availability. Inspector recommends having extra packs of test strips available to prevent future violations.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the seams of the wall paneling to be bubbling and separating. A white tape was used in areas to seal the seams, but this tape is already separating from the wall. Ensure the wall is repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Inspector observed the PIC describe inaccurate food handling procedures in the facility. The PIC stated that oranges and other garnishes are not handled with gloved hands. The inspector also observed the PIC training new staff on beverage preparation. The PIC was observed bare handing cherries, edible flowers, and citrus garnishes during this training event. The person in charge is responsible for knowing, understanding, and accurately communicating proper food handling procedures to staff members in the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 regarding the PIC's knowledge of proper food handling practices in the facility.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(8) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include: (8) Describing the relationship between the prevention of foodborne illness and the management and control of the following: (a) Cross contamination, (b) Hand contact with READY-TO-EAT FOODS, (c) Handwashing, and (d) Maintaining the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT in a clean condition and in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed a container of frappe mix being stored inside the ice machine with the container touching the ice used for drinks. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the mix was moved to the cooler. Ensure that food - in this case the ice that goes into drinks - is protected from cross contamination by keeping it separate from other food items and food packaging. Ice used for drinks should not be used for cold holding other food items.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed mold accumulation in the following areas: 
(Repeat) 1) The bar soda gun. 

Discussed with PIC, soda gun was cleaned with a sanitizing solution. Ensure soda guns are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer line was adjusted and dish machine tested at 100ppm CL. Ensure facility is monitoring dish machine to ensure sanitizer levels are at the proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The following food contact surfaces were observed with the accumulation of soil buildup. 
1. The baffles of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of pink mold.
2. The internal surface of the tea and coffee makers were observed to have a buildup of soil.

Discussed with PIC. All food contact surfaces mentioned were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) The following facility maintenance issues were observed.
1. The tile trim in the utility closet was observed coming off the wall. 
2. (REPEAT ) An accumulation of grease and food debris were observed under the fryers and grill in the kitchen. 
 PIC was made aware. Ensure that the accumulation is cleaned and trim sealed properly providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

 Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Multiple wet mop heads were observed stored on the floor on the utility closet including in the draining pit. Discussed with PIC. PIC instructed a staff member to remove the mop heads and have them stored properly. Ensure that proper mop storage procedures are followed at all times.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Inspector observed missing Employee Health Reporting Agreements for two of the three staff members who were present during today’s inspection. All staff who work in a food establishment must be informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report food-borne illness symptoms and diagnoses to their employees. Inspector will verify compliance on 6/1/26. Ensure all staff read and sign Employee Health Reporting Agreements within 30 days of hire, to be maintained on file for inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: The inspector observed the basin of the back of house hand washing sink to contain a bucket and cleaning supplies. CORRECTED- the inspector moved the items to wash hands. Education occurred with the Person in Charge (PIC) regarding hand sink availability. All designated hand washing sinks must be used for hand washing only.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 3 cans of food dented along the seams. CORRECTED- items were removed from service. Ensure all hermetically sealed containers are inspected for bulging, rust, and dents along the seams to prevent the entry and harborage of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: A large quantity of foods that are either temperature control for food safety (TCS) or labeled “keep refrigerated” were observed to have an internal temperature between 46-60F in the open air cooler. Foods include but are not limited to: calzones, deli sandwiches, desserts with cream cheese icing, sandwiches, cottage cheese, hard boiled (and peeled) eggs, cheesewiches, Naked juice, and pickles (labeled “keep refrigerated”). In addition, a pallet of Simply Juices labeled “Keep refrigerated” was stored at room temperature in dry storage. CORRECTED- items in the open air cooler were removed from service, and the PIC ensured the inspector that all foods and drinks aforementioned would be discarded after logging waste. All TCS foods (including those labeled “keep refrigerated”- the label is the law) under cold holding must be at or under 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens that cause food-borne illnesses.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: The mocha iced coffee bag was observed without date marking. CORRECTED- the inspector asked the PIC when the coffee bag was opened. PIC stated the bag was opened two days ago, and marked the bag with the corresponding date. Once TCS foods that are ready to eat and require cold holding are opened, they must bear date mark to be used or discarded within 7 days time.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the open air cooler to be failing to hold TCS foods at an internal temperature of 41F or below (see violation #22). Inspector recommends having the machine serviced to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. All cold holding units must have the capacity to maintain safe food temperatures. Inspector will return on 6/1/26 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed two stem thermometers 5-8F out of calibration. CORRECTED- the inspector modeled calibration using the ice water method to the PIC. Ensure all thermometers are maintained to be calibrated according to the manufacturer's instructions to provide accurate internal temperatures for TCS foods.
citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets of multiple standing coolers to be in disrepair. The following coolers need their gaskets repaired or replaced. Those housing: water, Gatorade, Celsius, Alani/ Bang, Monster (both) , and Mountain Dew. Ensure these repairs take place by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed build up on multiple nonfood contact surfaces:
1) A significant accumulation of ice in the blue bunny sliding freezer. Defrost and remove build up.
2) Soil debris on the outside of the ice shoots (soda stations).
Nonfood contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, and prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a wet mop stored in the basin of the mop bucket. CORRECTED- education was conducted and the mop was positioned to air dry. Mops function to clean up fats, oils, and greases- therefore must be placed in a position to air dry immediately after use to prevent the harborage of bacteria.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: At least three shelves inside of the walk in cooler were observed with dried debris. The shelves are used to store food, while some food items were uncovered and could possibility be exposed to cross contamination. Discussed and shown to the PIC. Ensure that shelves are taken outdoors to be power washed and cleaned to remove the unwanted debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There is a bit of ice build up on the floor underneath the shelves of the indoor walk in cooler (shelves mentioned in violation #49). Shown to the PIC. Ensure that the ice is removed and that the cooler is maintained free of ice accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There was grease buildup observed along the floor and the wall behind the cookline in the kitchen area. Shown to the PIC. Be sure that a cleaning schedule is in place to ensure that employees are frequently cleaning hard to reach areas (behind cookline) to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The ceiling along the cook-line is observed to have an accumulation of flour on the tiles and light covers. There is observed to be flour coming from the ceiling onto food-contact surfaces and into the batter stations. This is a potential for cross contamination. This violation is still present today. The PIC stated that they are working on cleaning the ceiling. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 (combined with the scheduled follow up for violation #47) to ensure that the ceiling along the cook-line has been cleaned to prevent cross contamination to food.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Two cans of Jalapeño cheese sauce were observed to be dented. PIC was made aware. The cans were removed from the inventory and stored separately to be returned. Ensure that all food product with compromised package integrity are removed from stock to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
FOLLOW UP REPEAT:
(i) The baffles of the hood system were previously coated with grease as to be observed with hanging debris. The operator has since the last inspection replaced 7 of 8 baffles with brand new baffles, with the 8th baffle to be replaced shortly.
(ii) There is dust and grease hanging from the Ansul system. See that the hood duct work is cleaned. The operator has scheduled hood maintenance for the end of May.
Inspector will Follow Up on 1 June 2026 to check that the hood has been cleaned.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: On arrival there was not a CFPM available on site. Ensure that a CFPM is available on site at all times that they are in operation.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: A food handler was observed to change gloves without hand washing. Education conducted.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The temporary hand washing station is observed in the hand sink on arrival and is deem not easily accessible. It was moved so the inspector could wash their hands and then m oved back after. Education conducted. Ensure that the hand washing set up is easily accessible to promote hand washing.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Various items that are packaged in house lacked specific label information. These items included packaged breads, veggies, seafood, etc. in many coolers, freezers, and shelves throughout the facility. Discussed with the PIC the required label information: common name of food, list of ingredients, name and place of business of manufacturer/distributor, and food source for each major food allergen. Ensure that the necessary information is included on packaged labels.
citation_text: 3-602.11(A) Food Labels. (A) FOOD PACKAGED in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, shall be labeled as specified in LAW, including 21 CFR 101 - Food labeling, and 9 CFR 317 Labeling, marking devices, and containers.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

An employee phone was observed on the cutting board of a prep cooler. A cut eggplant and knife were observed next to it as well as other foods being prepared. The PIC was shown and removed the phone to correct. The cutting board was sanitized as well. Ensure that employee belongings do not become a concern for contamination of foods and equipment.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair in the following locations:
1) The kitchen hand sink caulking was observed to be coming apart. 

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed no soap available at the bar handwashing sink. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) placed hand soap at the sink, to be hung from a hook moving forward (also discussed installing a soap dispenser- as long as it is available and functional, it is in compliance with the food code). Ensure hand washing sinks are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels to allow for proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed staff failure to use a barrier to shut off the faucet after handwashing. Discussed with PIC and education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to use a barrier to shut the faucet after handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The internal surface of the dish machine in the kitchen was observed with a buildup of soil accumulation. 
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the above mentioned surfaces would be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned are monitored, cleaned, sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The temperatures of the cut veggies in the prep cooler in the serving area were observed out of the appropriate range. PIC told inspector that all the food items in the unit may have been placed in the unit between last night and 9:00 AM today. The carrots were measured at 54 F and Celery was measured at 53 F.  The carrots (two trays) and celery (two trays and half a bag) were tossed. Ensure that chopped ready to eat food items are held within the appropriate temperature range to avoid bacteria growth.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler holding vegetables in the serving area was observed to not be holding temperature. The ambient temperature in the unit using an infrared thermometer was 61. The food items probed in the unit was temped at 53.5 on average. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the unit will be repaired within the follow-up timeframe. Ensure that the temperature of cold holding units are checked on a regular basis.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed a couple boxes of food items being stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. The boxes were removed to be stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to avoid contamination through splash at all times.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the top of the kitchen dish machine to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning dish machine at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with black debris. The PIC was informed and plans to deep clean/sanitize the machine. Ensure the ice machine is clean to sight and touch prior to the follow-up scheduled on 5/28/2026.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following physical facilities in need of repair:
1. There is a hole in the wall near the door of the dry storage area.
2. There is a hole in the wall near the back door of the facility.
3. The wall behind the soda syrup boxes is damaged and brittle. 

Ensure these areas are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored directly above grapefruit in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed and the eggs were relocated. Ensure proper storage order is followed to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods (fruit pizza between 67-68F) above 41F. CORRECTED- items were moved to time as control- to be used or discarded within 4 hours. Items failing to hold below 41F must be used or discarded by the end of the day's market.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Current cold holding methods (hard sided cooler with not enough cold packs and cooler tray) are failing to hold TCS items below 41F. Discussed ice baths or using many more cold packs. Inspectors will check for compliance at the 5/23/26 market.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: Inspector observed no disinfectant available for bodily fluid clean up. Obtain bleach or another disinfectant by 5/26/26 to ensure disinfectant is available to minimize the spread or contamination of food, food contact surfaces, employees, or consumers by vomit or fecal matter.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Food handler training
comment:
One employee who was present did not have a Food Handler's certificate available during today's inspection. All employees handling food must be certified as either a food handler, or certified food protection manager. Obtain necessary paperwork to be made available by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

1) The hand sink in the back of the facility was without paper towels during this inspection. 2) (REPEAT) The men’s bathroom was missing paper towels. Paper towels were supplied during the inspection to correct. Ensure all handwashing sinks are provided with hot running water, soap, and paper towels at all times.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

An open bag of hot dogs was observed in the walk in cooler without a date. This facility should not be serving any hot food per their risk classification. The hot dog package was likely opened in relation to the 4/10/26 inspection violation and should have been discarded at that time. The PIC was shown and discarded the package during this inspection to correct.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
(REPEAT from the Pre-Opening) 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

On arrival open boxes of foods were observed on the floor in the walk in freezer. This situation was noted on the previous inspection and is being placed here at this inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to stored the cases of food on the available shelves moving forward.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. 

Only quat test strips are available in the facility and only CL (bleach) sanitizer is available. The situation was discussed and the PIC was instructed to get new test strips prior to the follow-up.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a ready for use sanitizer available in the facility. When asked about wiping the counter for coffee or drink spill the PIC indicated that they use a spray Windex cleaner and towel. This is not acceptable and will need to be changed. Education was conduced and a solution utilizing CL was produced to correct the immediate violation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT from the Pre-Opening) 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

1) Repair damaged cabinet laminate. Exposed particleboard should be sealed. 2) Replace acoustic ceiling tiles over the drinks station and over the back of the soda fountain with smooth easily cleanable vinyl ceiling tiles. 3) Caulk countertops to backsplash at drinks station. These situations were discussed with the PIC and owner at the pre-opening and were reviewed during this inspection. Correct prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT from the Pre-Opening) 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

These items are still in violation from the pre-opening: 1) Clean floors under the back of the soda fountain and under shelving in the walk-in cooler. 2) Clean fan covers in the walk-in coolers. These locations were shown to the PIC and they are instructed to clean these areas and maintain them clean moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Water is observed leaking from the ceiling at two separate locations in the customer area of the building. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace the damaged tiles and the ceiling to prevent new damage from accruing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The ceiling along the cook-line is observed to have an accumulation of flour on the tiles and light covers. There is observed to be flour coming from the ceiling onto food-contact surfaces and into the batter stations. This is a potential for cross-contamination. A follow up will be conducted on 5/21/2026 to ensure that the ceiling along the cook-line has been cleaned to prevent cross contamination to food.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The lemonade nozzle on both soda machines in the facility were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- Both nozzles were cleaned during the inspection and this was discussed with both PICs. Ensure that soda nozzles are being cleaned frequently enough to prevent the accumulation of soil residue.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There are multiple dipping sauces that state to “Keep Refrigerated” that are being held at room temperature. These sauces are stored in the walk-in cooler until they are needed and are stored in a container in the drive-through at room temperature. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that these sauces were placed on the counter at around 9am and the sauces were voluntarily discarded due to being kept past the allowed 4 hours under Time as Control. These sauces will be stored in the bottom of the preparation cooler going forward. Ensure that Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food items are stored at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The walk-in cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 46F to 49F. Chicken was probed to be at 48F and 49F. This was discussed with the PIC, who stated that the walk-in cooler was checked at 9am that morning and was at 38F. The chicken that was delivered that morning was moved into the walk-in freezer and the other TCS items that were recently delivered were moved into other coolers. CORRECTED- The following items were probed and voluntarily discarded during the inspection: 
1. 4 pans of chicken (4 bags of classic and 4 bags of boneless): 47F and 48F. 
2. Multiple boxes of sauces, including buttermilk ranch (48F) and 8 boxes of blackened ranch (48F). 
3. Tartar sauce (48F). 
4. 1 box of havarti cheese (47F). 
5. 1 bag of shredded cheddar cheese (47F). 
6. 2 boxes of cabbage (49F). 
All other TCS food items that were within the proper temperature range were moved into another cooler or the walk-in freezer. The PIC stated that there is a company on the way to repair the walk-in cooler. Ensure that other TCS food items are not put into the walk-in cooler until it is properly holding temperature at 41F and below. Ensure that TCS food items are properly cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: In the batter stations, raw chicken probed to be at 52F and egg wash probed to be at 56F. The batter stations rely on ice baths for proper cold holding and there was no ice observed underneath the pans of food. The ice machine in the back of the kitchen is not functioning, according to the PIC, and they have to use the lobby ice machine for their ice baths. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that ice had been added under the pans only an hour before this. Ice was added to the water underneath the pans. Egg wash was probed to be at 41F and chicken was probed to be at 39F. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there is always plenty of ice and water to submerge the bottom of the pans to allow for proper cold holding of 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The walk-in cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 46F. There were multiple TCS food items that were discarded (see violation #22). The facility only has one preparation cooler and one standing cooler besides the walk-in cooler. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 to ensure that the walk-in cooler has been repaired and is properly cold holding at 41F and below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There are single-use boats sitting above the fryer with their food contact surfaces exposed to contamination. Discussed proper single service storage. Ensure that all single-service utensils and articles are inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: According to the PIC, the ice machine in the back of the facility is not functioning and they are waiting on a switch to repair it. Ice baths are used for cold holding for the batter stations and these were observed to not be properly cold holding during today’s inspection (see violation #22). Without the ice machine in the kitchen, they have to rely on the soda machines for ice. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 to ensure that the ice machine has been repaired or replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. THIRD REPEAT- The dish shelves across from the ice machine are rusted. The shelves either need to be sealed or replaced to prevent contamination to clean dishes. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The drain of the sanitizer compartment of the triple sink is observed to have an issue where even if it is closed, there is a slow leak coming from it. The facility is using a stopper in place of using the drain handle. Ensure that this issue is repaired to prevent the need for a stopper. The triple sink should be in good repair. 
3. SECOND REPEAT- There is ice build-up on the walk-in freezer pipes on the fan unit. Ensure that this ice is scraped off and that the issue causing the ice build up is repaired. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair or replaced as needed.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of being cleaned: 

1. The walk-in cooler fan covers were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. 
2. The floor in the walk-in cooler is observed to have a spill in the back of it and needs to be cleaned. 
3. The shelves in the walk-in cooler are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. 
4. The mop sink and the walls around it need to be cleaned. There were a few flies observed in this area. Ensure that this area is being cleaned frequently to prevent pest harborage conditions. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are being cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There are two drains in front of the fryers and batter stations that are observed to not be draining. A follow up is scheduled for 5/21/2026 to ensure that the drains have been repaired and are properly draining. Educate staff to keep drain covers on drains and to prevent grease from going down the drain to avoid future back-ups or cloggings.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. SECOND REPEAT- The front drink station in the drive through is observed to be in need of being sealed to the wall. Ensure that this is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. There are multiple holes in the wall above the handwashing sink behind the batter station. Ensure that these holes are sealed and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
3. The NUDO board is observed to need to be sealed behind the soda syrups and the carbonation tank. 
4. There is coving that is observed to need to be re-sealed to the wall across from the carbonation tank. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. All repairs should be made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the current method of cold holding to be insufficient (cheese surface temperature 68F). CORRECTED: Display cheese will not be sold to the consumer. citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:

1. The stainless steel sheet sealing the edge of the wall behind the hand sink by the drinks station.

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm QUat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available and at the proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed water bottles to be stored outside of gas station. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage of bottle and water will be moved inside. Ensure items are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink didn't have water available, nor was the hot water tank functional. There was a potable water source on site that provided clean water to the storage tank, however, the water heater remained unfunctional. SCDPH will follow-up on the mobile unit's next operating event for warm water for handwashing.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket was tested at 100ppm (quat). The employees mentioned that solution was provided by the dispenser at the brick and mortar. Discussed that the concentration was too low and needed to be at least 200ppm to properly sanitizer food contact surfaces. The inspector was able to get more Sani tablets from a different vendor to add to the concentration to correct the violation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: The chlorine sanitizer being used is a lavender scented variant. The PIC was instructed to have non-scented sanitizer prior to the next routine inspection. Inspectors will follow up either at the 6/25/26 at Rochester Sports in the Park.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: An employee drink is observed mixed in with the single service boats. The drink was moved to correct.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket on the preparation line was observed to have a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The PIC remade the sanitizer bucket using Quaternary ammonium sanitizer tablets and it tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Discussed making sure to routinely test the concentration and change the bucket if it is not at the label-recommended concentration. This should typically be done every two to four hours.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. comment: There were containers of blue sea cream dated 5/2, which is past the 7-day allotted date-marking, that the PIC stated is made in-house. title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility had a Chlorine sanitizer bucket in use, but did not have any Chlorine test strips. The facility has Quaternary ammonium sanitizer tablets and test strips. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that they will cease use of Chlorine as a sanitizer and use the Quaternary ammonium sanitizer that they have. Discussed making sure that if Chlorine is used again in the future that Chlorine test strips will be obtained.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The counter holding the tea containers is observed to be in disrepair and needs replaced or the bare wood needs to be sealed. 
2. The triple sink and the bathroom sinks are observed to be in need of being re-sealed. 

These repairs were discussed with the operator. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed that establishment is using a multi-purpose cleaning bleach for food-contact surface sanitizer, and not an appropriate bleach product for food-contact surfaces. PIC was informed, and should acquire the proper sanitizing product by the Follow Up date of 18 May 2026. Times to wash hands include but are not limited to: before donning gloves, after using using the restroom, between working with raw and ready to eat foods, etc.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed cooked rice holding an internal temperature of 114F. CORRECTED- the item was moved under TIME AS CONTROL (TAC)- the item was stated to have been prepared at 11 AM, and will be used or discarded by 3PM. Once rice (or noodles, or vegetables) are cooked they become temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods- and therefore must be held below 41F or above 135F to prevent the growth of pathogens. Ensure all TCS foods are kept outside of the temperature danger zone.
